Only the new `NumberUtilsAgentTest.java` was added — no other files were touched (the pre-existing deletion of `NumberUtilsTest.java` was already there before I started).

## Summary

Created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/math/NumberUtilsAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 5 test class (matching the project's `org.junit.jupiter.api` style, no extension of `AbstractLangTest` or import of `LangAssertions`) covering `NumberUtils`'s public API: constants, `compare`, `createBigDecimal/BigInteger/Double/Float/Integer/Long/Number`, `isCreatable`/`isNumber`/`isDigits`/`isParsable`, all `max`/`min` overloads (array and 3-arg, all 6 numeric types) including null/empty boundary errors, `toByte/Double/Float/Int/Long/Short` (with and without defaults), and all `toScaledBigDecimal` overloads.

Tricky `createNumber` behaviors (hex/octal parsing, type suffixes, Float-vs-Double-vs-BigDecimal selection, sign-position errors) were verified against actual runtime behavior via a throwaway probe program before writing assertions, rather than guessed.

Verified with `mvn test -Dtest=NumberUtilsAgentTest`: **71 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors**.
